content.title: About
content.content: Moscow Mule is a cocktail made with vodka, ginger beer, and fresh lime juice, traditionally served in a copper mug. It originated in the United States in the early 1940s as a marketing effort to boost ginger beer sales and quickly became a bar classic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Moscow Mule was created in 1941 at the Cock ’n’ Bull bar in Los Angeles.
The name references Moscow, although the original recipe uses American vodka.
The iconic copper mug not only looks striking but also chills the drink rapidly, enhancing the ginger beer aroma.
Moscow Mule is often perceived as a “female” cocktail, yet it enjoys popularity across all demographics.
Since the 2020s, many variations have appeared: Gin Mule, Mexican Mule (with tequila), and a non‑alcoholic Virgin Mule.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Lime juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and offers antioxidant protection.

items.title: Ginger beer has anti‑inflammatory properties
items.content: Ginger is known for its anti‑inflammatory and digestive benefits, helping to ease nausea.

items.title: Moderate hydration
items.content: Because the majority of the drink is non‑alcoholic ginger beer, it can contribute to overall fluid intake.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Lime and ginger beer supply potassium, important for blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Moscow Mule contains vodka, so it should be consumed responsibly, especially by individuals with alcohol contraindications.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Commercial ginger beers often contain high amounts of sugar, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Ginger may irritate the stomach
items.content: In some individuals, ginger can cause heartburn or stomach irritation.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Lime may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the Moscow Mule in a chilled copper mug that has been pre‑cooled in the freezer. Combine 50 ml vodka, 15 ml fresh lime juice, and top up with ginger beer. Garnish with a sprig of mint or a lime wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep opened ginger beer refrigerated and seal the bottle tightly. Store vodka in a cool, dark place. Clean copper mugs with a soft cloth, avoiding abrasive cleaners to preserve the finish.
